transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
Well… since I stopped working, I just can’t seem to slow down much. I’m up and moving all day, going from one little job to the next, like there’s still a crew waiting on me or something.
Do you feel like you have to do these little jobs or is it more that you just can't seem to stop moving?
More like I can’t stop moving, I guess. Since I stopped working, I’m just… up all day, going from one small job to the next. Feels like I still ought to be keeping things going.
Do you ever feel like you're thinking about something over and over that you can't get out of your head?
Not really, no. I mean, I think about things, sure, but not like… stuck on one thought that won’t leave.
Do you find yourself doing things on impulse, without fully thinking them through?
Sometimes, yeah. In those storytelling meetings, I’ll jump in with an answer before the other person’s even finished. Then I notice I’ve cut them off, and… I feel bad about it.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're sitting still?

Yeah… I do. If I’m sitting through something quiet, like a meeting or a church talk, I start shifting around or tapping my foot. Sometimes I feel like I need to get up and stretch, even when I know I’m supposed to just sit there.
Are these behaviors and feelings of restlessness causing problems for you in your daily life or relationships?

Yeah… a bit. My wife’s had to kind of take over the calendar and check behind me on things. And I’ve had to apologize more than once to folks at the community center and the garden group when I’ve let them down. So… yes, it causes some problems.
Do you feel restless or have trouble sitting still in all situations, or are there certain places or activities where you can relax and stay still?

It’s not all the time, no. If it’s quiet and I’m supposed to sit still—like a meeting or a church talk—that’s when I notice it. I’ll shift around, tap my foot, feel like I need to get up and stretch. Other times I can be okay.
Did you notice these feelings of restlessness and inability to slow down starting after you stopped working?
Yeah… it did seem to get more noticeable after I stopped working. I retired from handyman work about a year and a couple months ago, and that’s when it started feeling like more of a real problem.
Have you noticed your restlessness or impulsive behaviors affecting your relationships with friends and family?

Yeah… mostly with my wife, I guess. She’s had to take over the calendar and kind of check behind me. And outside the house, I’ve had to apologize a few times to the community center and the garden group when I didn’t follow through.
How much distress do these feelings of restlessness and impulsive behaviors cause you?
I don’t know… I’d say it bothers me some, but I wouldn’t call it overwhelming. Mostly it’s frustrating when I notice I’m doing it, or when someone points it out.
Do you often find it hard to focus on what someone is saying to you?
I’m not really sure. I mean, sometimes I miss things, but I haven’t noticed it as a big pattern when someone’s talking to me.
Do you often find yourself easily distracted by things around you?
Yeah, I guess so. If I’m trying to paint or work out a story and there’s a truck outside… or I suddenly think about something in the garden, my mind kind of goes there, and I lose my place.
Did you have trouble paying attention or following instructions when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. Back in grade school, teachers would say I was bright, but kind of scattered. I remember losing pencils a lot, blurting out answers, and needing reminders to finish my work before recess.
Do you have difficulty finishing tasks or projects that you start at home or in your hobbies?

Yes… that does happen. My wife might ask me to fix the gate, sweep the porch, and put the tools away, and I’ll get the gate only half done, then end up pulling weeds or something. Then the rest just sits there.
Did you have trouble paying attention in class or following instructions from teachers when you were in school?
Yeah… I did. Teachers used to say I was bright, but scattered. I’d lose pencils, call out answers, and they had to remind me to finish my work before recess.
Did you have more problems with behavior, like acting out or disobeying rules, when you were a child?
I don’t really know. I mean, I wasn’t trying to be a bad kid or anything. I don’t remember getting into serious trouble much… maybe just normal kid stuff.
Were you fidgety, restless, or having trouble paying attention when you were a little kid, before you turned 12?
Yeah… I guess so. In grade school they’d say I was bright, but kind of scattered. Losing pencils, blurting out answers… and needing reminders to finish my work before recess.
Do you think you had these problems with restlessness and paying attention before you were 7 years old?

Yeah… I think so. I don’t remember it perfectly, but even in early grade school teachers were already saying I was bright but scattered—losing pencils, calling out answers, needing reminders to finish my work.
Have your symptoms of restlessness and impulsive behaviors significantly interfered with your ability to function in daily life or maintain relationships since you stopped working?

Yeah… I suppose it has, some. My wife’s had to kind of take over the calendar and check behind me. And I’ve had to apologize a few times at the community center and the garden group for dropping the ball on things.
Have you had these feelings of restlessness and trouble paying attention your whole life, or did they start later?

I think it was always there, pretty much. Even back in grade school, teachers would say I was bright, but scattered… losing pencils, calling out answers, needing reminders to get my work done before recess.
